criteria.title: Informative images have a text alternative
Decorative images are ignored by assistive technologies
Text alternatives of informative images are relevant
CAPTCHA and test images have an alternative identifying their nature and function
CAPTCHAs have an alternative access solution
Informative images have a detailed description if needed
Detailed descriptions of images are relevant
Images of text are replaced by styled text if possible
Image captions are correctly linked to their images
Frames have a title
Frame titles are relevant
Information is not conveyed by color alone
Contrast between text and background is sufficient
Interface components and informative graphics have sufficient contrast
Prerecorded time-based media have a transcript or an audio description if needed
Transcripts and audio descriptions of time-based media are relevant
Prerecorded synchronized media have synchronized captions if needed
Synchronized captions are relevant
Prerecorded time-based media have a synchronized audio description if needed
Synchronized audio descriptions are relevant
Time-based media are clearly identifiable
Non-time-based media have an alternative if needed
Alternatives to non-time-based media are relevant
Automatically triggered sounds can be controlled by the user
Time-based media can be controlled by keyboard and any pointing device
Non-time-based media can be controlled by keyboard and any pointing device
Media are compatible with assistive technologies
Complex data tables have a summary
Summaries of complex data tables are relevant
Linearized content of layout tables remains understandable
Data table titles are correctly associated with their tables
Data table titles are relevant
Row and column headers of data tables are correctly declared
Data table cells are correctly associated with their headers
Layout tables do not use data table elements
Links are explicit
Links have a name
Scripts are compatible with assistive technologies if needed
Alternatives to scripts are relevant
Scripts can be controlled by keyboard and any pointing device
Users are warned of or control script-initiated changes of context
Status messages are correctly rendered by assistive technologies
Each page has a document type
Generated source code is valid for the document type
The default language is present
The default language code is relevant
Each page has a title
Page titles are relevant
Language changes are indicated in the source code
Language codes of language changes are valid and relevant
Tags are not used for presentation only
Changes in reading direction are indicated
Information is structured by appropriate headings
The document structure is consistent
Lists are correctly structured
Quotations are correctly indicated
Style sheets are used to control the presentation of information
Visible informative content remains present without style sheets
Information remains understandable without style sheets
Text remains readable when enlarged up to 200%
CSS declarations of text and background colors are used correctly
Links whose nature is not obvious are visible within the surrounding text
Focus is visible on each focusable element
Hidden content is meant to be ignored by assistive technologies
Information is not conveyed by shape, size or position alone
Information conveyed by shape, size or position is also conveyed relevantly by other means
Content can be presented without scrolling in two dimensions
Text spacing can be overridden without loss of content or functionality
Additional content shown on hover or focus can be controlled by the user
Additional content shown with CSS can be displayed by keyboard and any pointing device
Form fields have a label
Form field labels are relevant
Labels of fields with the same function are consistent
Labels are adjacent to their fields
Fields of the same nature are grouped if needed
Groups of fields have a legend
Legends of field groups are relevant
Items of the same nature in choice lists are grouped relevantly
Button labels are relevant
Input validation is used relevantly
Input validation offers suggestions to correct errors if needed
Users can modify, update or retrieve data entered in forms with significant consequences
The purpose of input fields can be determined to support autofill
Each set of pages has at least two different navigation systems
Menus and navigation bars are always in the same place
The sitemap page is relevant
The sitemap page is reachable through an identical feature
The search engine is reachable in an identical way
Content regions present on several pages can be reached or skipped
A skip link or quick access link to the main content is present
The tab order is consistent
Navigation contains no keyboard trap
Single-key keyboard shortcuts can be controlled by the user
Additional content shown on hover, focus or activation is reachable by keyboard
Users control each time limit that changes content
New windows do not open without user action
Downloadable office documents have an accessible version if needed
Accessible versions of office documents offer the same information
Cryptic content has an alternative
Alternatives to cryptic content are relevant
Sudden changes in brightness and flashing effects are used correctly
Moving or blinking content can be controlled by the user
Content can be viewed in any screen orientation
Features using complex gestures are also available with simple gestures
Actions triggered by a single pointer can be cancelled
Features triggered by device motion can be operated otherwise
